title: ATM inhibition attenuates ferroptosis-associated injury and reduces infarct volume in experimental stroke

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《ATM inhibition attenuates ferroptosis-associated injury and reduces infarct volume in experimental stroke》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · P9】To bridge the gap between the previous cancer cell line study and future translation, we investigated the therapeutic potential of ATM inhibition by AZD1390 using various preclinical ex vivo and in vivo models of ischemic stroke. Here, we show that ATM inhibition using AZD1390 not only limits ferroptosis in vitro but also significantly reduces neuronal cell death in both ex vivo organotypic brain slice models and in vivo mouse models of ischemic stroke. AZD1390 treatment reduced infarct volume, and this protection was accompanied by reduced ferroptosis-associated lipid peroxidation. Additionally, we reveal that there is significant variation in AZD1390 efficacy among different inbred mouse strains, and this variation is associated with the extent of the collateral vascular network, which critically affects drug delivery to the ischemic territory. These results highlight not only the molecular and translational potential of AZD1390, but also the determinants of therapeutic response, facilitating individualized stroke treatments. These results underscore the therapeutic potential of targeting ferroptosis pathways as a physiologically relevant and promising translation pathway for ischemic stroke in humans.

【Aims · abstract-1-1】Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death, contributes to neuronal injury after ischemic stroke. Because our previous cancer-cell screens identified ataxia-telangiectasia mutated (ATM) kinase, as a ferroptosis regulator, we investigated whether ATM inhibition protects neural tissue after ischemic stroke and examined determinants of therapeutic response.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《ATM inhibition attenuates ferroptosis-associated injury and reduces infarct volume in experimental stroke》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Study design and methodological rigor. · P26】All experimental group sizes were established based on prior experience and statistical power consideration. Both male and female animals were included across the in vivo studies to account for sex as a biological variable. Group allocations included either equal representation (e.g., n = 6 total per group, consisting of 3 males and 3 females) or approximately equal, balanced distributions across sexes in larger groups (e.g., up to n = 17 per group); exact sex distributions for each group are detailed in the Supplemental Table. For in vitro and ex vivo assays, experiments were performed with a minimum of n = 3 independent biological replicates per group. Animals were randomly assigned to the treatment or control group prior to procedures. Investigators were blinded to experimental conditions, treatment arms, and surgical groups during data collection and analysis. Pre-established exclusion criteria were defined for technical failures or non-completion of experimental protocol. However, no animals were excluded from the final analysis, and all raw data were fully reported. All units and chemical concentrations throughout the manuscript were thoroughly corrected for accuracy.

【Supplementary Material · P40】The supplementary material for this article is available at: Supplementary materials.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《ATM inhibition attenuates ferroptosis-associated injury and reduces infarct volume in experimental stroke》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusion · P39】This study implicates ferroptosis-associated lipid oxidative injury in neuronal cell death after ischemic stroke, highlighting ATM inhibition, particularly with the brain-penetrant AZD1390, as a promising therapeutic strategy. By showing that ATM inhibitors reduce neuronal cell death and infarct volume in both ex vivo and in vivo models, this research supports further investigation of ferroptosis as a therapeutic target in stroke. The efficacy of AZD1390, an orally bioavailable and brain-penetrating clinical compound, underscores its translational relevance. These findings pave the way for the development of ferroptosis-targeting therapies to mitigate neuronal injury and improve clinical outcomes for stroke patients, offering a pathophysiologically grounded approach with clinical feasibility.

【Results · abstract-3-1】ATM inhibition reduced ferroptosis-associated lipid oxidative injury and protected neurons in multiple preclinical stroke models. AZD1390 decreased lipid peroxidation and neuronal death, and reduced infarct volume in B6/J and B6/NJ mice, but not in BALB mice. Treatment efficacy varied among strains and was correlated with collateral vascular density. Systemic AZD1390 was likewise ineffective in Rabep2-knockout mice with deficient collateral networks. Early topical administration also reduced infarct volume in mice with limited collateral networks; however, differences in treatment timing and route preclude direct attribution to improved local drug delivery.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《ATM inhibition attenuates ferroptosis-associated injury and reduces infarct volume in experimental stroke》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Figure 1. · F1】Figure 1. AZD1390 protects against erastin-induced ferroptosis in MDA-MB-231 cells. (a) ATM inhibitors protect MDA-MB-231 cells against ferroptosis. MDA-MB-231 cells were treated with increasing doses of erastin (24 h), either alone or in combination with liproxstatin-1 (LPT1, 2 μM), KU55933 (5 μM), and KU60019 (1 μM). Cell viability was quantified by CellTiter-Glo assay; (b, c) AZD1390 reduced erastin-induced ferroptosis in MDA-MB-231 cells in a dose-dependent manner. After 24 hours of incubation, cell viability and cytotoxicity were determined by CellTiter-Glo assay (b) and CellTox Green assay (c), respectively. Canonical ferroptosis inhibitors: Fer-1; DFO; (d, e) Erastin-induced lipid peroxidation (10 μM, 18 hours) in MDA-MB-231 cells was reduced by AZD1390; Lipid peroxidation was assessed by C11-BODIPY staining (d) and quantified as the percentage of lipid peroxidation-positive cells (e). (a, b, and e) Data represent the mean ± SEM. (a, b) 2-way ANOVA and Dunnett’s multiple comparisons. (e) One-way ANOVA followed by Dunnett’s multiple comparison test. (c) Non-parametric Mann-Whitney tests with correction for multiple comparisons. Data represents the median ± IQR. (a-e) n = 6 independent biological replicates. *p < 0.05; **p < 0.01; ***p < 0.001, ****p < 0.0001. MDA: malondialdehyde; ATM: ataxia-telangiectasia mutated; LPT1: liproxstatin-1; Fer-1: Ferrostatin-1; DFO: Deferoxamine; SEM: standard error of the mean; ANOVA: analysis of variance; IQR: interquartile range.

【Figure 2. · F2】Figure 2. AZD1390 increases neuronal cell viability in the cortical brain slice ischemia assay. (a, b, and c) Representative images showing YFP-transfected cortical pyramidal neurons in rat brain slices under non-OGD control conditions (a), after 4.5 minutes of OGD (b), and after 4.5 minutes of OGD followed by Fer-1 treatment (1 μM) (c). Scale bar, 100 μm; (d) Effects on neuron cell viability following OGD: treatment with the ferroptosis inhibitor Fer-1 and the indicated ATM inhibitors, including AZD1390, significantly increased cell viability; (e, f) AZD1390 reduced the induction of ferroptosis markers, SLC7A11(e) and PTGS2 (f), in the rat brain slice model of ischemic stroke. Transcript levels of SLC7A11 (e) and PTGS2 (f) were measured using qPCR from the rat brain slices. n = 6 independent biological replicates; (g) Neuronal cell viability in mouse brain slices increased in a dose-dependent manner with AZD1390 treatment. Each gray point in panels d and g represents the neuronal-viability measurement from one individual hemi-coronal brain slice. Twelve slices were analyzed per condition in each independent experiment, and three independent experiments were performed, resulting in 36 slice-level observations per condition. The slices were obtained from 12 animals per experiment and randomly distributed across treatment conditions. Individual slice-to-animal identities were not retained. (d, e, and g) Data represent the median ± IQR. Kruskal-Wallis test with Dunn’s multiple comparison (*p < 0.05; **p < 0.01; ***p < 0.001, ****p < 0.0001). (f) Data represent the mean ± SEM. One-way ANOVA followed by Dunnett’s multiple comparison test. OGD: oxygen glucose deprivation; Fer-1: Ferrostatin-1; ATM: ataxia-telangiectasia mutated; qPCR: quantitative PCR; IQR: interquartile range; SEM: standard error of the mean; ANOVA: analysis of variance.

【Figure 3. · F3】Figure 3. AZD1390 reduces infarct volume after pMCAO in an in vivo stroke model. (a) Schematic timeline illustrating the experimental procedure, including ischemic stroke induction through pMCAO and AZD1390 treatment; (b) Serial brain slice sections (1 mm) from the B6/NJ inbred mouse strain. Infarcted tissue appears as white after 2% TTC staining. Scale bar: 5 mm; (c) The graph showing infarct volume 72 hours after pMCAO includes both vehicle-treated control groups (black bar with plots) and AZD1390-treated groups (red bar with plots) for each inbred strain: B6/J, B6/NJ, and BALB. 2-way ANOVA and Šídák’s multiple comparisons (****p < 0.0001); (d) AZD1390 decreased MDA levels in brain tissues from mice subjected to pMCAO followed by vehicle or AZD1390 treatment. The antibody targeting MDA recognized all MDA-modified proteins in brain tissues at different molecular weights. GAPDH was used as a loading control. Each lane represents brain tissue from one individual animal. The vehicle samples are identified as V1-V7, and the AZD1390-treated samples as A1-A7. Samples V1-V4 and A1-A4 were analyzed on one membrane, whereas samples V5-V7 and A5-A7 were analyzed on a second membrane, as indicated by the vertical dividing line. MDA-modified proteins and the corresponding GAPDH loading controls are shown from the same samples. Uncropped images of both membranes, including molecular-weight markers, are provided in Figure S3. Complete sample identities are provided in Table S1; (e) All bands of MDA-modified proteins in each lane were quantified using ImageJ. Quantification was of MDA levels normalized to GAPDH. Data represent the mean ± SEM and statistical significance was determined by two-tailed Student’s t-test (*p < 0.05). pMCAO: permanent middle cerebral artery occlusion; TTC: 2,3,5-triphenyltetrazolium chloride; ANOVA: analysis of variance; MDA: malondialdehyde; SEM: standard error of the mean.
